# What Is interface.ai, and What Does It Cost? (2026 Guide)

[![Abbas, Customer Support & AI, Macha](https://www.getmacha.com/images/authors/abbas.jpg)](https://www.getmacha.com/authors/abbas)

Written by

[Abbas](https://www.getmacha.com/authors/abbas) [Abbas on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mabbasmad/)

[![Ankeet Guha, Co-founder & CTO, Macha](https://www.getmacha.com/images/authors/ankeet.jpg)](https://www.getmacha.com/authors/ankeet)

Reviewed by

[Ankeet Guha](https://www.getmacha.com/authors/ankeet) [Ankeet Guha on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ankeetguha/)

Updated October 6, 2026

interface.ai builds AI voice, chat and employee agents only for credit unions and community banks, and claims more than 100 of them as customers handling over 1.5 million conversations a day. Its pricing is unpublished, so the named case studies are the best evidence a buyer has.

## Key takeaways

- interface.ai sells AI voice, chat and employee agents only to credit unions and community banks, and publishes no pricing, sending every visitor to book a demo.
- interface.ai's homepage claims 100+ credit union and community bank customers, 1.5 million-plus conversations a day, 99.99% uptime, 100+ languages and over 40 integrations.
- Radiant Credit Union reports interface.ai Voice AI handles 31,700 calls a month at 67% containment while assets grew from $500 million to $800 million.
- interface.ai launched Smart Collections in February 2026 and Nexus, an agentic contact center platform for credit unions and community banks, on 15 April 2026.
- For a team whose workload is a help desk ticket queue rather than banking calls, Macha is the done-for-you option: the Macha team sets up and runs the agent, at about $0.40 a ticket including a dedicated success manager.

![What Is interface.ai, and What Does It Cost? (2026 Guide)](https://www.getmacha.com/images/grid/6aabf704887505fa9b60a4c2?w=1200&q=80)

interface.ai sells AI voice, chat and employee-assist agents only to credit unions and community banks, under its BankGPT platform, and it publishes no pricing: every path on its site ends at "Book a demo." Its homepage claims 100+ credit union and community bank customers and 1.5 million-plus conversations a day. It doesn't chase retail, travel, or general enterprise contact centers.

| interface.ai at a glance | As of 24 September 2026 |
| --- | --- |
| **Built for** | Credit unions and community banks only |
| **Products** | Voice AI, Chat AI, Employee AI, Smart Collections, Nexus contact center, fraud prevention |
| **Pricing** | Not published; demo and sales-led |
| **Free trial** | None published |
| **Languages** | 100+ (homepage) |
| **Integrations** | Over 40, including banking cores, CRMs and payment gateways |
| **Best named result** | Radiant Credit Union: 31,700 calls a month at 67% containment |

## What is interface.ai?

![interface.ai's homepage: "Agentic AI for personal finance," with 100+ credit union customers.](https://www.getmacha.com/images/grid/6aabf5c4c8571c78e612f335?w=900)interface.ai's homepage: "Agentic AI for personal finance," with 100+ credit union customers.

interface.ai describes its platform, branded **BankGPT**, as agentic AI purpose-built for credit unions and community banks, delivering "a 24/7, multilingual AI financial expert" across voice, digital, and employee-assisted channels. The company was bootstrapped until October 2024, when it closed a funding round led by Avataar Venture Partners that [Fintech Futures](https://www.fintechfutures.com/ai-in-fintech/interface-ai-emerges-as-most-valuable-ai-company-in-banking-with-avataar-led-30m-funding-round) reported at $30 million. Its own homepage reports **100+ credit unions and community banks**, **1.5 million-plus conversations a day**, and **99.99% uptime**.

Two launches in 2026 widened the product. **Smart Collections** (25 February 2026) is a collections agent that automates early-delinquency outreach across voice and other channels. **Nexus** (15 April 2026) is what interface.ai calls a fully agentic contact center (CCaaS) platform, meant to remove hold queues and transfers for credit unions and community banks.

The platform organizes its agents into three groups: **Voice AI Agents** (phone-based support and fraud checks), **Digital AI Agents** (chat and self-service), and **Employee Augmentation Agents** (internal tools for frontline staff), wrapped around four functions the company calls Automation, Augmentation, Authentication, and Fraud Prevention. That fraud and authentication focus is specific to banking in a way a general contact-center AI vendor's feature list usually isn't: caller ID forensics, device biometrics, voice biometrics, SIM swap and spoofing detection, and account velocity detection all sit inside the same platform diagram as the conversational agents.

![interface.ai's platform diagram: Voice, Digital, and Employee Augmentation Agents in one hub.](https://www.getmacha.com/images/grid/6aabf5c7c8571c78e612f339?w=900)interface.ai's platform diagram: Voice, Digital, and Employee Augmentation Agents in one hub.

## What results do named interface.ai customers report?

interface.ai's site leans hard on aggregate homepage statistics (100+ institutions, 1.5 million conversations a day, and "140M Americans in our market", which is a market size rather than a count of people served), and separately publishes individual case studies with specific, attributed numbers. Worth treating those two tiers differently.

**Radiant Credit Union**, founded in 1953 and based in North Central Florida, reports its Voice AI now handles 31,700 calls a month at 67% containment. Radiant grew from about $500 million to $800 million in assets, a 60% increase, without expanding the contact center, avoiding an estimated four additional hires. A membership merger with First Coast Community Credit Union on 1 June 2026 then pushed combined assets past $1 billion. **Dupaco Community Credit Union** (Dubuque, Iowa, founded 1948, 160,000-plus members) reports deploying interface.ai's Voice AI specifically for fraud prevention and 24/7 member support, freeing agents to focus on more complex member needs.

![interface.ai's Dupaco Community Credit Union case study, on fraud prevention and service.](https://www.getmacha.com/images/grid/6aabf66b88bc085003098a52?w=900)interface.ai's Dupaco Community Credit Union case study, on fraud prevention and service.

**Bank of Guam** (Hagatna, Guam, founded 1972, 160,000-plus customers) reports deploying both Voice AI and Chat AI to manage rising contact volumes with a lean team, describing the goal as scaling support "without compromising care." These named case studies, tied to a specific institution's founding date and member count, are a meaningfully stronger form of evidence than an aggregate homepage stat with no attribution behind it.

![Bank of Guam's case study: "Taps Generative AI to Scale Digital-First Support."](https://www.getmacha.com/images/grid/6aabf66e88bc085003098a55?w=946)Bank of Guam's case study: "Taps Generative AI to Scale Digital-First Support."

## What are interface.ai's key features?

- **Voice, Digital, and Employee Augmentation Agents** from one platform, instead of separate point tools for each channel.
- **Banking-specific fraud and authentication tooling**: caller ID forensics, device and voice biometrics, SIM swap detection, spoofing detection, and account velocity checks built into the same agent stack that handles routine conversations.
- **100+ languages** and what the company describes as over 40 integrations, connecting to the banking cores, CRMs and payment gateways credit unions already run.
- **Nexus and Smart Collections**: a 2026 agentic contact-center platform and a collections agent, both sold to the same banking buyer.
- **BankGPT platform positioning**: a single underlying system, instead of separately branded voice and chat products bolted together.

## How much does interface.ai cost?

interface.ai does not publish pricing anywhere on its site; the pricing URL returns a 404, and every call to action leads to "Book a demo." That's standard for banking-core-adjacent software sold to credit unions and community banks, where procurement usually runs through a formal RFP process instead of a self-serve signup.

We have no reliable published number or third-party estimate to cite for interface.ai specifically. Given the platform's integration depth into core banking systems and its focus on fraud and authentication (higher-stakes, higher-compliance functionality than a generic chatbot), budget for an enterprise-grade sales and integration cycle, similar in shape to other banking-core-adjacent software, on top of any monthly usage rate.

The incentive worth naming: selling exclusively to credit unions and community banks, skipping the broader enterprise contact-center market, means interface.ai's roadmap and pricing structure are built around a buyer that moves slowly and cares enormously about compliance and fraud liability. That's a reasonable trade for the target customer, but it also means the sales cycle looks nothing like signing up for a self-serve SaaS tool.

## What do actual users say about interface.ai?

We could not produce a confident real-user product rating for interface.ai. G2's reviews page returned a 403 to direct access, and Gartner Peer Insights did the same. A search for interface.ai's rating mostly surfaced Glassdoor and RepVue results, which measure employee satisfaction working at the company instead of customer satisfaction with the product, so we're not citing those as product reviews here.

That gap is worth naming plainly instead of papering over with an unrelated number: interface.ai's named case studies (Radiant, Dupaco, Bank of Guam, and others in its published library) are the strongest public evidence available, and they read as credible specifically because they're attributed to a real, checkable institution instead of an anonymous quote.

## Pros and cons

**Pros**

- Named, attributed case studies from real credit unions with specific figures, not just aggregate marketing statistics.
- Banking-specific fraud and authentication tooling built into the same platform as the conversational agents, not sold as a bolt-on.
- Deep specialization in one industry, with 100+ credit unions and community banks as customers and over 40 integrations into the systems they already run.
- Well funded ($30M raised) for the scale of institution it's built to serve.

**Cons**

- No published pricing anywhere, and no reliable third-party estimate exists to fall back on.
- No accessible independent review platform (G2 and Gartner Peer Insights both blocked automated access), so a prospective buyer is working almost entirely from interface.ai's own case studies.
- Narrow by design: it's built for banking. A retailer, travel company, or general enterprise contact center gets no benefit from the fraud and core-banking integrations that are the product's main differentiator.
- Aggregate homepage statistics and attributed case-study results sit side by side without always being clearly distinguished, worth checking carefully during a sales conversation.

## Who is interface.ai best for?

interface.ai fits teams at a credit union or community bank that need voice and chat support built around real banking workflows, balance inquiries, fraud checks, authentication, loan questions, rather than a generic FAQ bot repurposed for finance. The named case studies include credit unions growing from $500 million past $1 billion in assets, suggesting the platform scales across a meaningful range within that specific industry.

It's the wrong choice for anyone outside banking. A retailer or a SaaS support team gets zero value from SIM-swap detection or core-banking integrations, and the sales-led, RFP-shaped buying process makes no sense for a team that wants to self-serve a trial this week.

## How does interface.ai compare with Kore.ai and Macha?

![Kore.ai's homepage, "AI Agents proven to deliver your outcomes," with customer logos.](https://www.getmacha.com/images/grid/6aabf5c8c8571c78e612f33c?w=900)Kore.ai's homepage, "AI Agents proven to deliver your outcomes," with customer logos.

The closest comparison is [Kore.ai](https://kore.ai/), a broader enterprise conversational AI platform that also serves banking and financial services among many industries, rather than specializing in it exclusively. Kore.ai also publishes no pricing page, consistent with enterprise, sales-led software in this category generally.

|  | interface.ai | Kore.ai | Macha |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Model** | Banking-exclusive voice, chat, and employee AI (BankGPT) | Broad enterprise conversational AI across industries | AI agent layer on your existing help desk |
| **Best for** | Credit unions and community banks specifically | Enterprise contact centers across many verticals | Teams on Zendesk, Freshdesk, Gorgias, Front, HubSpot or Intercom |
| **Pricing** | Unpublished, sales-led | Unpublished, sales-led | From $299/mo for 750 tickets (~$0.40/ticket), published |
| **Fraud/authentication tooling** | Built into the core platform | Available via broader enterprise configuration | Standard controls; scoped per agent |
| **Self-serve trial** | No | No | $50 free usage |
| **Replaces your help desk?** | No general ticket queue; layers onto core banking, and its Nexus platform (2026) can run the contact center itself | No, layers onto an existing CCaaS/CRM stack | No, sits on top of Zendesk, Freshdesk, Gorgias, Front, HubSpot or Intercom |

The real choice between interface.ai and Kore.ai for a bank or credit union is depth versus breadth: interface.ai builds only for banking and goes deep on fraud and core integrations, while Kore.ai serves banking as one of several verticals on a more general platform. For our detailed take on Kore.ai specifically, see our guide to [Kore.ai](https://www.getmacha.com/blog/kore-ai-complete-guide). Neither vendor touches a support team's ticket queue in a [help desk](https://www.getmacha.com/product/macha-on-helpdesk); that's where [Macha](https://www.getmacha.com/pricing) fits, as an AI agent layer inside Zendesk, Freshdesk, Gorgias, Front, HubSpot or Intercom. Macha is the [done-for-you option](https://www.getmacha.com/done-for-you): the Macha team analyzes your past tickets, builds the knowledge base and the agent, and runs it in safe mode until the drafts are right, at about $0.40 a ticket, which includes setup and a dedicated success manager who handles your changes. For more on how vertical AI platforms compare to help-desk-native agents generally, see our guide to [AI agents for customer service](https://www.getmacha.com/blog/ai-agents-for-customer-service).

The other vendor built exclusively for this market is [Posh AI](https://www.getmacha.com/blog/posh-ai-complete-guide), which sells to credit unions and community banks on much the same pitch, so it is worth pricing alongside interface.ai rather than after it. If you want the wider enterprise option in the same detail, our [Kore.ai guide](https://www.getmacha.com/blog/kore-ai-complete-guide) covers its platform, pricing and review data.

## How we researched this

interface.ai's site blocked direct automated fetches (403) across every page we tried, so we used a rendered browser capture instead, which returned the same public content a visitor sees. Its sitemap confirmed real case-study URLs for Radiant, Dupaco, Bank of Guam, and others, which we captured directly. No pricing page exists on the domain. G2 and Gartner Peer Insights both blocked review access; the only "interface.ai reviews" we could surface through search were Glassdoor and RepVue employee reviews, which we're not citing as product feedback. Kore.ai's homepage was captured the same way for the comparison.

## FAQ

**What is interface.ai?** interface.ai builds AI voice, chat, and employee-assist agents specifically for credit unions and community banks, branded as the BankGPT platform, with built-in fraud detection and authentication tooling alongside conversational support.

**How much does interface.ai cost?** interface.ai doesn't publish pricing, and no reliable third-party estimate exists. Expect an enterprise sales and integration cycle typical of banking-core-adjacent software rather than a self-serve monthly rate.

**Is there a free trial?** No self-serve trial is published. Every path on the site leads to booking a demo.

**What results do interface.ai customers report?** Radiant Credit Union reports its Voice AI handles 31,700 calls a month at 67% containment, and that it grew from $500 million to $800 million in assets without expanding the contact center, before a June 2026 merger took it past $1 billion. Dupaco Community Credit Union and Bank of Guam report similar deployments for fraud prevention and 24/7 member support. These are named, vendor-published case studies.

**Does interface.ai only work with credit unions?** Its case studies and platform positioning focus exclusively on credit unions and community banks; it isn't marketed for retail, travel, or general enterprise support.

**What are good alternatives to interface.ai?** Kore.ai is the closest comparison for banks and credit unions that want a broader enterprise conversational AI platform rather than a banking-exclusive one. For support teams running a single help desk instead of a full banking-core stack, a lighter, help-desk-native AI agent is a better fit than either vendor.

**Does interface.ai replace a help desk?** Not a general one. It layers onto a credit union or bank's core banking system, and since April 2026 its Nexus platform is pitched as a replacement contact center for banking calls. It has no general-purpose ticket queue for non-banking support use cases.

**Does interface.ai have good reviews?** We couldn't confirm through an independent review platform. G2 and Gartner Peer Insights both blocked automated access, and no independent product-review sample was reachable at the time of writing; the strongest public evidence is interface.ai's own named case studies.
